title: Mastering Penetrating Keratoplasty: From Trauma to Graft Survival
summary: This comprehensive guide explores the management of full-thickness corneal trauma, the complexities of Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP) procedural complications, and the critical pre-operative assessment and risk stratification necessary for graft success.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation: Corneal Laceration
sections.content: A1: This is a limited Anterior Segment photo showing normal lids and conjunctiva, a linear central horizontal scar in the cornea with multiple small vertical scars of old approximating sutures. The possible etiology here is a full thickness corneal laceration.

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Step 1: Clinical assessment of visual potential.
Step 4: Surgical intervention: Optical Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP) if vision remains poor.

rows: Scleral perforation, donor damage (trephine reversal), retained Descemet’s, iris-lens damage, AC haemorrhage, suprachoroidal expulsive haemorrhage
Wound leaks (Seidel+), epithelial defects, filamentary keratitis, suture-related (infection/infiltrates/Kaye dots), Glaucoma, Anterior Synechiae, Pupillary block, Urrets-Zavalia pupil
Graft failure (immunologic/poor donor/trauma/HSV), Immunologic rejection (Epithelial/Subepithelial/Endothelial/Diffuse), Post-operative astigmatism

sections.title: Pre-operative Assessment Protocol
content: History: Past BCVA, Age of Insult, Ocular Alignment, Projection of rays
Ocular Surface: Dry eye evaluation (TBUT, Schirmer), Conjunctival Inflammation
Cornea: Size and depth of scar, Vascularization
AC Status: PAC, Lens status, Vitreous in AC

sections.title: Risk Stratification & Prognostic Indicators
content: High Risk Factors: Young age, Repeat Grafts, Large graft (>8mm), Eccentric graft, PAS, Deep stromal vascularisation, High IOP, Ocular surface disease, Uveitis, Active herpetic inflammation.

Poor Prognostic Host Factors: Severe stromal vascularization, absence of corneal sensation, extreme thinning at host-graft junction, active inflammation, lid abnormalities, recurrent conjunctival inflammation (SJS, OCP).
Favorable Cases: Keratoconus, localized scars, and dystrophies.

content.explanation: Kaye dots (epithelial, donor side) are non-pathologic. Immune infiltrates require intensive steroids and suture removal. Khodadoust line (endothelial rejection) is a medical emergency requiring intensive/IV steroids. Large grafts (8-8.5mm) carry significantly higher rejection risk.
